posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
@mrnoobs
Those tiles are paired for a reason - the A4 tilesheet has one row of ceiling tiles above one row of wall tiles, repeated three times.
They are intended to go over the other, with the ceiling tiles being walkable on specific rules to simulate a two-level-dungeon on a one-level-map.
So depending on what exactly you want to do on your map, it might be better to move the tile you want to use to A2.
That said, two tips in general:
1) if you have to post a resource from someone else, try to make it unusable to others first. For example grey-scaling it etc.
2) if you're asking about a specific part of a multipart-sheet, it helps if you mark it with arrows or circles. Because there are several tiles that could be called "wires" in that sheet.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
And why did you remove the picture of the tilesheet itself?
Now we can't compare where you went wrong with the autotiles.
If you're talking about the borders to your fences - that is normal and intended behaviour. And to remove them you don't need any tile edit, you just need to learn how to use shift-click-mapping, one of the most important techniques on using the map editor.
It would be much better if you understand how to use autotiles before trying to make your own tiles...
please search the forum - there should be several tutorials on shift-click mapping.
An older one is linked in my starting point tutorial (see signature)
